title: Tromba marina (marine trumpet)
summary: The tromba marina, or marine trumpet, is a bowed instrument of medieval and baroque Europe with one long string stretched over a tall, tapering wooden body that stands about as high as a person. The player does not press the string to a fingerboard. A fingertip rests lightly on it at points where it divides evenly, bringing out the bright natural notes, while one foot of the bridge buzzes against the soundboard to give the sound of a trumpet.
howToPlay: One long string runs the whole length of the body. Each lane marks a point where it is touched lightly, the lowest note first.
A bead slides down the string to the point. Touch and bow as it lands.
The notes are the natural series, so the steps get smaller as you rise.
Learn the phrase by echo, then play it through with the pulse.
rules: The notes are the natural series of one string, from the open string to the eighth partial.
A stroke on the beat is perfect, a near one is good, and extra strokes cost points.
Figures are written for this game in the style of the tradition.
heritageNote: The tromba marina was played in European towns and courts from the fifteenth to the eighteenth century. The single long string, the tall tapering body and the buzzing bridge foot that gives its trumpet voice are its signature.
